 Judgment

Respondent No.2-insurer is impugning the judgment and award dated 06.09.2021 passed in MVC.No.88/2011 on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and Member Additional M.A.C.T.,
Iterinary Court, Byadagi (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of conveyance.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the legal representatives of the deceased Subash Sanganavar filed MVC.No.88/2011 before the Tribunal claiming compensation for the death of the deceased,
contending that he died in a road traffic accident on 27.11.2010 while he was proceeding on his TVS two wheeler, the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-27/T- 5166 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed to the two wheeler as a result of which the rider sustained injury and died in the hospital.
Claimants being the mother, brothers and sisters of the decease were dependent on his income and claimed compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending tractor-trailer have filed objections denying the claim of the claimants.
The insurer contended that the claimants are not entitled for any compensation.

5. On the basis of these pleadings, the following issues were came to be framed;

6.
The claimants examined PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P7 in support of their contentions.
Respondents have not led any oral evidence.

The copy of the insurance policy is marked as Ex.R1.
7.
The Tribunal after taking into consideration all these materials on record awarded compensation of Rs.6,17,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
8. Being aggrieved by the same, the respondent No.2-insurer is before this Court.
9. Heard Smt. Preeti Shashank, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. Chandrashekar M.Hosamani, learned counsel for the respondents.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side.
The claimants include mother, brothers and sisters of the deceased and age of the mother was taken into consideration.
The income of the deceased was taken up at Rs.3,000/-.
Even though there are no materials to substantiate the same.
Only 1/5th of the income was deducted towards his personal expenses even though the deceased was a bachelor.
Therefore she submits that the amount awarded by the Tribunal was on higher side and hence same is to be reduced to award just compensation.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents opposing the appeal contended that the claimants being the dependents have led evidence before the Tribunal.
It has taken into consideration the materials on record and awarded just compensation.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Perused the materials on record.
13.

In view of the above, the point that would arise for my consideration is;
Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal requires interference of this Court?

14. My answer to the above point is in the negative for the following;
REASONS 15.
It is noticed that the claimants who are mother, brothers and sisters of the deceased are said to have been dependent on the deceased.
The Tribunal after taking into consideration of the oral document evidence formed an opinion that the deceased who was aged 28 years was earning Rs.3,000/- per month.
The same cannot be held to be exorbited, but it is reasonable.

sentences.text: Only 1/5th of the amount is being deducted towards the personal expenses.
The Tribunal has assigned valid reasons while awarding the compensation.
I do not find any perversity or illegality in the findings recorded by the Tribunal and also the quantum of compensation awarded.
Hence, I am of the opinion that there are no grounds made out to interfere the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

Hence, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed with costs.
The amount in deposit, if any, is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
